sentences.zh: 存在这种区别

sentences.en: when the Noyce came back after the Supreme Court ruling,
sentences.zh: 但当最高法院裁决后噪音卷土重来时

sentences.en: Black defendants were actually among those
sentences.zh: 黑人被告实际上是其中

sentences.en: who were the most severely harmed by this.
sentences.zh: 受害最深的人群之一。

sentences.en: Is it possible in some ways
sentences.zh: 在某些方面，噪音和偏见之间

sentences.en: there can be intersections between Noyce and Bias?
sentences.zh: 是否存在某种交集呢？

sentences.en: In other words, they can amplify one another?
sentences.zh: 换句话说，它们会相互放大吗？

sentences.en: Certainly.
sentences.zh: 当然会。

sentences.en: I mean, when you are constraining people and reducing noise,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当你约束人们并减少噪音时

sentences.en: you're reducing the opportunities for bias to take place.
sentences.zh: 你也就减少了偏见产生的机会。

sentences.en: So attempts to reduce noise
sentences.zh: 因此，减少噪音的尝试

sentences.en: and attempts to control noise
sentences.zh: 以及控制噪音的尝试

sentences.en: are going to, in general, not invariably,
sentences.zh: 通常（虽然并非总是如此）

sentences.en: but are very likely to control and reduce bias as well.
sentences.zh: 也非常有可能同时控制和减少偏见。

sentences.en: If noise produces many of the adverse outcomes we see,
sentences.zh: 如果噪音导致了我们所看到的许多不良后果

sentences.en: if noise produces much of the unfairness we see,
sentences.zh: 如果噪音导致了我们所看到的许多不公

sentences.en: why is it that critiques of disparities
sentences.zh: 为什么对差异的批评

sentences.en: invariably talk about bias?
sentences.zh: 总是谈论偏见呢？

sentences.en: Turns out, that's because of the way our minds work.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，这是因为我们大脑的运作方式。

sentences.en: As we discussed in a recent series of episodes,
sentences.zh: 正如我们在最近的一系列节目中所讨论的那样

sentences.en: the brain is a storytelling machine,
sentences.zh: 大脑是一台讲故事的机器

sentences.en: and the story of bias
sentences.zh: 而关于偏见的故事

sentences.en: caters to our hunger for simple explanations.
sentences.zh: 迎合了我们对简单解释的渴望。

sentences.en: I mean, clearly, bias in general is a better story.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，显然，偏见通常是一个更好的故事。

sentences.en: That is, you see something happening.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，你看到某事发生了。

sentences.en: It had the character of an event.
sentences.zh: 它具有某种事件的特征。

sentences.en: It had the character of something that is caused
sentences.zh: 它具有某种由某种心理力量

sentences.en: by a psychological force of some kind.
sentences.zh: 所驱动的特征。

sentences.en: Variability, noise, is uncaused.
sentences.zh: 而变异性，即噪音，是无缘无故的。

sentences.en: Noise doesn't lend itself to a causal story.
sentences.zh: 噪音本身并不适合编成因果故事。

sentences.en: And really, the mind is hungry for causes.
sentences.zh: 而人类的心智确实渴望因果关系。

sentences.en: And that leads us very naturally to think in terms of biases.
sentences.zh: 这很自然地引导我们从偏见的角度去思考。

sentences.en: That errors must be explainable.
sentences.zh: 认为错误必须是可以解释的。

sentences.en: So if I get a misdiagnosis because a doctor doesn't like the color of my skin,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我因为医生不喜欢我的肤色而遭到误诊

sentences.en: that might not make me feel good,
sentences.zh: 这可能让我感觉不好

sentences.en: but at least I can make sense of what happened.
sentences.zh: 但至少我能理解发生了什么。

sentences.en: Once I settle on an explanation of racism or sexism or homophobia,
sentences.zh: 一旦我认定这是种族主义、性别歧视或恐同症的解释

sentences.en: I tell myself I have every right to get angry.
sentences.zh: 我就会告诉自己，我有充分的理由感到愤怒。

sentences.en: When I discuss what happened with others,
sentences.zh: 当我与他人讨论这件事时

sentences.en: they'll get angry too.
sentences.zh: 他们也会感到愤怒。

sentences.en: By contrast, a misdiagnosis produced by noise is,
sentences.zh: 相比之下，由噪音导致的误诊

sentences.en: by definition, no one's fault.
sentences.zh: 从定义上讲，是谁的错都不是。

sentences.en: The error may have harmed me,
sentences.zh: 错误可能伤害了我

sentences.en: but I can't lay the blame on someone's evil intentions.
sentences.zh: 但我无法将责任归咎于某人的恶意。

sentences.en: Noise is the very opposite of a good story.
sentences.zh: 噪音与好故事恰恰相反。

sentences.en: It's meaningless.
sentences.zh: 它是毫无意义的。

sentences.en: And that can make me feel even worse.
sentences.zh: 这反而可能让我感觉更糟。

sentences.en: Here's another problem.
sentences.zh: 这里还有另一个问题。

sentences.en: When I see a judge pass a really harsh sentence or a very light sentence,
sentences.zh: 当我看到法官做出非常严厉或非常轻的判决时

sentences.en: I can come up with a story of bias to explain this individual case.
sentences.zh: 我可以编造一个关于偏见的故事来解释这个个案。

sentences.en: You cannot do that with noise.
sentences.zh: 但你无法用噪音来做到这一点。

sentences.en: You cannot spot noise by looking at any individual case.
sentences.zh: 你无法通过观察任何个案来发现噪音。

sentences.en: You have to measure it in the aggregate.
sentences.zh: 你必须在总体上进行衡量。

sentences.en: It shows up only when you look at the statistics.
sentences.zh: 它只有在你查看统计数据时才会显现出来。

sentences.en: And many of us are uncomfortable turning to data as our guide to the truth.
sentences.zh: 我们许多人并不习惯将数据作为寻求真理的指南。

sentences.en: We prefer stories and anecdotes.
sentences.zh: 我们更喜欢故事和轶事。

sentences.en: And stories and anecdotes are better at illustrating the problem of bias.
sentences.zh: 而故事和轶事在说明偏见问题上确实更有效。

sentences.en: Stories and anecdotes are what the mind is prepared for.
sentences.zh: 故事和轶事是人类心智所准备好的东西。

sentences.en: Statistical thinking is alien to us.
sentences.zh: 统计思维对我们来说是陌生的。

sentences.en: And statistical thinking is the only way to detect noise because it's variability.
sentences.zh: 而统计思维是检测噪音的唯一方法，因为它是一种变异性。

sentences.en: It's sort of absurd to say about any single case that it is noisy.
sentences.zh: 说任何单一案例是“嘈杂的”都是荒谬的。

sentences.en: You say that if you have no idea how it came about.
sentences.zh: 如果你根本不知道它是如何产生的，你才会这么说。

sentences.en: But noise is a phenomenon that you observe statistically and that you can analyze only statistically.
sentences.zh: 但噪音是一种你只能通过统计观察并进行统计分析的现象。

sentences.en: And that is not appealing.
sentences.zh: 而这并不吸引人。

sentences.en: So, there's an even deeper problem than the fact that noise is detectable only through statistics, whereas bias, you know, you can tell a story about bias.
sentences.zh: 所以，这里有一个比“噪音只能通过统计检测，而偏见可以编成故事”更深层的问题。

sentences.en: For many people making decisions, the data is simply not even available.
sentences.zh: 对于许多做决策的人来说，数据根本就不可用。

sentences.en: So, at a statistical level, you can say an insurance company is demonstrating noise.
sentences.zh: 所以，在统计层面上，你可以说一家保险公司表现出了噪音。

sentences.en: But many of the decisions we are making are decisions we make as individuals.
sentences.zh: 但我们做出的许多决策都是以个人身份做出的。

sentences.en: So, if I want to propose marriage and I feel like proposing marriage on a moonlit night in the springtime,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我想求婚，并且觉得在春天的月光之夜求婚很有感觉

sentences.en: I have no idea if my decision to propose marriage on that evening is being shaped by noise or not.
sentences.zh: 我根本不知道我那天晚上求婚的决定是否受到了噪音的影响。

sentences.en: I don't have a statistical set of how I would behave under different circumstances.
sentences.zh: 我没有一套关于我在不同情况下会如何表现的统计数据。

sentences.en: You know, the truth of the matter is that no one can tell you that this decision was noisy.
sentences.zh: 你知道，事实是没人能告诉你这个决定是否充满了噪音。

sentences.en: What you can tell is that when you look at the collection of decisions of people deciding to get married, that collection is noisy.
sentences.zh: 你能知道的是，当你观察人们决定结婚的决策集合时，那个集合是充满噪音的。

sentences.en: There is no reason to believe that these steps, which improve judgments in the statistical case, do not apply when somebody decides to get married.
sentences.zh: 没有理由相信这些在统计案例中能改善判断的步骤，在某人决定结婚时就不适用了。

sentences.en: If noise is present in the decisions where you can observe it, it's also present when you cannot observe it.
sentences.zh: 如果噪音存在于你能观察到的决策中，那么它也存在于你无法观察到的决策中。

sentences.en: Some years ago, I interviewed the researcher Berkley DietworSt.
sentences.zh: 几年前，我采访了研究员伯克利·迪特沃斯特（Berkley DietworSt）。

sentences.en: He talked about how people respond when a mistake has been made by a human versus an algorithm.
sentences.zh: 他谈到了当人类与算法犯错时，人们会有何反应。

sentences.en: I want to play you a short excerpt of something he told me.
sentences.zh: 我想为你播放一小段他告诉我的内容。

sentences.en: People failed to use the algorithm after they'd seen the algorithm perform and make mistakes, even though they typically saw the algorithm outperform the human.
sentences.zh: 人们在看到算法运行并犯错后，就不再使用该算法了，尽管他们通常看到算法的表现优于人类。

sentences.en: In our studies, the algorithms outperform people by 25 to 90 percent.
sentences.zh: 在我们的研究中，算法的表现比人类好 25% 到 90%。

sentences.en: So he's basically saying the algorithms are significantly better than the humans.
sentences.zh: 所以他基本上是在说，算法明显优于人类。

sentences.en: But when a mistake is made, and algorithms, of course, can make mistakes and humans can make mistakes, he's saying that you prefer the human to make the mistake.
sentences.zh: 但当错误发生时——当然，算法和人类都会犯错——他说你更倾向于让那个人类去犯错。

sentences.en: And I think intuitively that feels correct to me.
sentences.zh: 我认为直觉上这对我来说是正确的。

sentences.en: If I'm going to get a misdiagnosis when I go to a doctor, I would feel better if it's the doctor who's made the mistake than an unfeeling, unthinking algorithm.
sentences.zh: 如果我去看医生时被误诊了，如果是医生犯了错，我会比被一个冷冰冰、没思想的算法误诊感觉好受些。

sentences.en: I think that's absolutely true.
sentences.zh: 我认为这绝对是真的。

sentences.en: And, you know, when we're looking at a road accident, we somehow feel less bad about it if it was a driver error than if it was a self-driving car that caused the accident.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，当我们看到一起交通事故时，如果是司机失误造成的，我们似乎比如果是自动驾驶汽车造成的事故感觉要好受一些。

sentences.en: Algorithms, they make errors.
sentences.zh: 算法，它们确实会犯错。

sentences.en: The errors they make, by the way, are different from the errors that people would make.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，它们犯的错误与人类犯的错误是不同的。

sentences.en: And they look stupid to people.
sentences.zh: 而且在人们看来，它们显得很愚蠢。

sentences.en: Algorithms make errors that people think are ridiculous.
sentences.zh: 算法犯的错误在人们看来是荒谬的。

sentences.en: Now, we don't get to hear what algorithms think of the errors that people make.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们听不到算法对人类所犯错误的看法。

sentences.en: And we do know that algorithms just make far fewer of them in many cases.
sentences.zh: 但我们确实知道，在许多情况下，算法犯的错误要少得多。

sentences.en: And you have to trade off the higher overall accuracy against the discomfort of abandoning human judgment and trusting an algorithm.
sentences.zh: 你必须在更高的整体准确性与放弃人类判断、信任算法带来的不适感之间进行权衡。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You know, this might actually be a subtext of much of your lifetime's work, Danny,
sentences.zh: 你知道，这可能实际上是你毕生工作的大部分潜台词，丹尼（Danny），

sentences.en: but it seems to me that fighting noise requires a certain amount of humility.
sentences.zh: 但在我看来，对抗噪音需要一定程度的谦逊。

sentences.en: And it seems to me that humans are not humble.
sentences.zh: 而且在我看来，人类并不谦逊。

sentences.en: Well, they're not humble for a fairly straightforward reason.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们不谦逊的原因很简单。

sentences.en: We do not go through life imagining different ways of seeing what we see.
sentences.zh: 我们不会在生活中去想象看待事物的不同方式。

sentences.en: We see one thing at a time.
sentences.zh: 我们一次只看一件事。

sentences.en: And it feels right to us.
sentences.zh: 而且我们觉得它是对的。

sentences.en: And, you know, that is really the source of the problem of ignoring noise.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这确实是忽视噪音问题的根源。

sentences.en: This is why it is so difficult to imagine it.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么想象它如此困难。

sentences.en: I want to talk just for a brief moment about places where noise can potentially be useful.
sentences.zh: 我想简短地谈谈噪音可能有用的一些地方。

sentences.en: So, let's say, for example, you have a company that's trying to innovate and come up with new ideas.
sentences.zh: 假设，例如，你有一家公司试图创新并提出新想法。

sentences.en: Or you're in a creative enterprise where you want to pitch different ideas for movies.
sentences.zh: 或者你身处一个创意企业，想要为电影推销不同的想法。

sentences.en: In some ways, you might want to actually maximize the variability of the ideas you get.
sentences.zh: 在某些方面，你可能实际上想要最大化你所获得想法的变异性。

sentences.en: So, noise is not always bad.
sentences.zh: 所以，噪音并不总是坏事。

sentences.en: Sometimes it can actually lead to good things.
sentences.zh: 有时它实际上可以带来好的结果。

sentences.en: Yeah, we don't call it noise in those cases.
sentences.zh: 是的，在这些情况下我们不称其为噪音。

sentences.en: So, we reserve the term noise for undesirable variability.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们将“噪音”一词保留给不可取的变异性。

sentences.en: There are indeed many situations in life in which variability is a blessing.
sentences.zh: 生活中确实有很多情况，变异性是一种福气。

sentences.en: Certainly in creative enterprises.
sentences.zh: 在创意企业中当然如此。

sentences.en: Also evolution.
sentences.zh: 进化也是如此。

sentences.en: So, anything that allows you to select the better one of multiple responses,
sentences.zh: 所以，任何允许你从多种反应中选择更好的一种的东西，

sentences.en: wherever there is a selection mechanism, variability is a good thing.
sentences.zh: 只要有选择机制的地方，变异性就是一件好事。

sentences.en: But variability in the absence of a selection mechanism is a sheer loss of accuracy.
sentences.zh: 但在缺乏选择机制的情况下，变异性纯粹是准确性的损失。

sentences.en: And those are the cases that we talk about.
sentences.zh: 而这些就是我们所讨论的情况。

sentences.en: So, if you had a way when you have multiple underwriters of finding out who is doing a better
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你有一种方法，当你有多个承保人时，能找出谁做得更好，

sentences.en: job than whom and using that in order to improve their training, that would be a case where you
sentences.zh: 并利用这一点来改进他们的培训，那将是一个你可以

sentences.en: could make positive use of variability.
sentences.zh: 积极利用变异性的案例。

sentences.en: But in the absence of such a mechanism, that variability just is a sheer loss.
sentences.zh: 但在缺乏这种机制的情况下，那种变异性纯粹就是损失。

sentences.en: When we come back, how to fight noise.
sentences.zh: 回来后，我们将讨论如何对抗噪音。

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 你正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》（Hidden Brain）。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆（Shankar Vedantam）。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: Noise is endemic.
sentences.zh: 噪音是普遍存在的。

sentences.en: It's also very difficult to fight, in part because judges and doctors and police officers
sentences.zh: 它也非常难以对抗，部分原因是法官、医生和警察

sentences.en: don't like to think of themselves as capricious.
sentences.zh: 不喜欢认为自己是反复无常的。

sentences.en: We don't think of our judgments as being arbitrary,
sentences.zh: 我们不认为我们的判断是武断的，

sentences.en: certainly not when it comes to really important decisions.
sentences.zh: 尤其是在涉及非常重要的决策时。

sentences.en: Even when we are told about how noise is affecting our judgments and decisions,
sentences.zh: 即使当我们被告知噪音是如何影响我们的判断和决策时，

sentences.en: we hate to be shackled by rules.
sentences.zh: 我们也不喜欢被规则束缚。

sentences.en: Danny, in 1907, Charles Darwin's cousin, Francis Galton, asked 787 villagers at a county fair
sentences.zh: 丹尼，1907 年，查尔斯·达尔文的表弟弗朗西斯·高尔顿（Francis Galton）要求乡村集市上的 787 名村民

sentences.en: to estimate the weight of a prize ox.
sentences.zh: 估算一头奖品牛的重量。

sentences.en: None of the villagers guessed the right answer.
sentences.zh: 没有一个村民猜出了正确答案。

sentences.en: But then Galton did something with their answers that got him very close to the correct answer.
sentences.zh: 但后来高尔顿对他们的答案进行了一些处理，使他非常接近正确答案。

sentences.en: What did he do, Danny?
sentences.zh: 丹尼，他做了什么？

sentences.en: Well, he simply took the average.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他只是取了平均值。

sentences.en: And the average, I think, was within two pounds of the correct weight.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，这个平均值与正确重量的误差在两磅以内。

sentences.en: And that led to a lot of research that was summarized in a recent book by James Surowiecki
sentences.zh: 这引出了詹姆斯·苏罗维基（James Surowiecki）最近在一本书中总结的大量研究，

sentences.en: on the wisdom of crowds.
sentences.zh: 关于“群体的智慧”。

sentences.en: And the fact that when you take multiple judgments, independent judgments,
sentences.zh: 事实上，当你收集多个独立的判断，

sentences.en: and average them, you eliminate noise.
sentences.zh: 并将它们平均化时，你就消除了噪音。

sentences.en: This, by the way, is guaranteed to eliminate noise.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，这在数学上保证能消除噪音。

sentences.en: So if you take multiple judgments, there is no guarantee that it will reduce bias,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你收集多个判断，并不能保证能减少偏差，

sentences.en: because if the judges agree on the bias, then the bias will remain when you take the average.
sentences.zh: 因为如果评判者在偏差上达成一致，那么当你取平均值时，偏差依然存在。

sentences.en: Indeed, it will be even more salient.
sentences.zh: 事实上，它甚至会变得更加突出。

sentences.en: But what is absolutely guaranteed is that when you average independent judgments,
sentences.zh: 但绝对可以保证的是，当你对独立的判断取平均值时，

sentences.en: you are eliminating noise.
sentences.zh: 你就是在消除噪音。

sentences.en: When you take 400 judges, you are reducing noise by one half.
sentences.zh: 当你采用400个评判者的意见时，噪音会减少一半。

sentences.en: When you take 100, you are reducing it by 90%.
sentences.zh: 当你采用100个时，噪音会减少90%。

sentences.en: So there is some mathematics of noise that lends itself to analysis that doesn't apply to bias.
sentences.zh: 所以，关于噪音的数学原理是可以进行分析的，而这并不适用于偏差。

sentences.en: So it's really remarkable.
sentences.zh: 这真的很了不起。

sentences.en: The correct weight of that ox was 1,198 pounds.
sentences.zh: 那头牛的正确重量是1198磅。

sentences.en: And as you said, that was one or two pounds off the correct weight.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，那与正确重量只差一两磅。

sentences.en: And I want to point out that the reason averaging the responses produces a better answer
sentences.zh: 我想指出的是，对回答取平均值能产生更好结果的原因，

sentences.en: is that noise is random.
sentences.zh: 在于噪音是随机的。

sentences.en: You're taking advantage of the fact that various estimates will be randomly high or low.
